newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slightly firmer ahead of NTMA auction.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slightly firmer ahead of NTMA auction.

text.p: Irish bonds were slightly firmer on Monday in dull trade ahead of Tuesday's auction by the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA), dealers said.
"We're dead in the water today in terms of volume, with people waiting for the auction," one dealer said. "There's no domestic news of any interest and other markets seem to be quiet as well."
The NTMA is set to auction 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent Treasury bond due 2006 at 1000 local time tomorrow (0900 GMT).
Dealers said they expected good investor interest in the bond - largely from domestic players - as it had outperformed in recent weeks, narrowing the spread over Germany.
"The 10-year bond has cheapened on the curve by about five basis points in the last five trading days and looks pretty attractive," a dealer said.
On Monday the 10-year spread over bunds in afternoon trading was at 89 basis points, while the five-year pick-up was at 143 basis points over Germany, dealers said.

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up four pence from Friday's close at 101.49 to yield 6.10 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up nine pence from the close at 107.77 to yield 6.84 percent.

Looking ahead, dealers said markets would focus on Tuesday's release of U.S. consumer prices data at 1230 GMT. The forecast is for a rise of 0.3 percent in March and for a rise of 3.0 percent year-on-year.

On Friday higher than forecast core producer prices and retail sales for March together with a big upward revision to Feburary retail sales heightened fears of near-term interest rate hikes and spooked markets around the globe.
Some volatility on other markets such as equities and currency may also affect bonds this week, analysts said.
